paper_cards.title: ESI-Bench: Towards Embodied Spatial Intelligence that Closes the Perception-Action Loop
paper_cards.data: OmniGibson-grounded benchmark with 10 task categories, 29 subcategories, and 3,081 embodied spatial questions that require perception, locomotion, and manipulation decisions.
paper_cards.method: recasts spatial intelligence as an active perception-action loop, evaluates embodied agents under controlled task families, and measures gains from active exploration versus passive observation.
paper_cards.task: answer embodied spatial questions that require choosing how to move, inspect, and manipulate the environment to uncover hidden spatial facts.
paper_cards.novelty: moves spatial intelligence benchmarking from passive or oracle-view settings into an embodied action loop where the agent must actively gather the evidence needed for reasoning.
paper_cards.evidence: Primary evidence comes from the arXiv paper, official project page, and official GitHub repository; benchmark scope, task taxonomy, and code availability are source-traced.

claim_checks.claim: ESI-Bench benchmarks embodied spatial intelligence through a perception-action loop rather than passive observation.
claim_checks.notes: Abstract explicitly frames spatial intelligence as active observation conditioned on action.

claim_checks.claim: The benchmark spans 10 task categories and 29 subcategories built on OmniGibson.
claim_checks.notes: Official project page states the task-category and subcategory counts.

claim_checks.claim: The benchmark contains 3,081 embodied QA tasks.
Official code and dataset are public.
claim_checks.notes: Official repository is public and linked from the project page.

paper_cards.limitations: Benchmark conclusions still depend on OmniGibson task design and evaluation scripts; this run did not re-execute the benchmark locally.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Strong benchmark reference for whether generated or reconstructed worlds preserve the active spatial structure needed for embodied decision-making.

paper_cards.title: EmbodiedGen V2: An Agentic, Simulation-Ready 3D World Engine for Embodied AI
paper_cards.data: sim-ready asset, scene, and task-world generation pipeline with public Hugging Face collection and dataset for cross-simulator embodied world construction.
paper_cards.method: unified generative world engine that composes sim-ready assets, editable scenes, task-driven worlds, dialogue-based state editing, and cross-simulator export into one closed-loop pipeline.
paper_cards.task: turn text, images, and dialogue instructions into executable multi-room 3D worlds that can be deployed across major simulators for embodied learning.
paper_cards.novelty: pushes embodied world generation from isolated assets toward a reusable, agentic world engine that keeps affordances, state, layout stability, and simulator interfaces aligned.
paper_cards.evidence: Primary evidence comes from the arXiv paper, official project page, public GitHub repository, video, Hugging Face collection, and public dataset links.

claim_checks.claim: EmbodiedGen V2 is framed as an agentic, simulation-ready 3D world engine for embodied AI.
claim_checks.notes: Title and abstract state the world-engine positioning.

claim_checks.claim: The system supports sim-ready assets, large-scale scenes, task-driven worlds, vibe coding, and cross-simulator export.
claim_checks.notes: Official project overview lists each stage explicitly.

claim_checks.claim: Official code, model collection, and dataset are public.
claim_checks.notes: Project page links GitHub, Hugging Face collection, and dataset.

paper_cards.limitations: This run verified the project surface and paper claims but did not execute the cross-simulator export or world-editing loops locally.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Very strong fit for the repository’s interactive generation branch because it connects asset generation, affordance/state retention, and executable world assembly.

paper_cards.title: Interactive World Simulator for Robot Policy Training and Evaluation
paper_cards.data: moderate-scale robot interaction dataset driving an action-conditioned video world model that supports multiple manipulation tasks and an interactive online demo.
paper_cards.method: uses consistency models for both latent dynamics prediction and image decoding to build a fast, stable action-conditioned world simulator for closed-loop robot policy training and evaluation.
paper_cards.task: simulate long-horizon robot interaction rollouts quickly enough and stably enough that policies can be trained and evaluated inside the learned world model.
paper_cards.novelty: targets the missing middle ground between slow pixel-rollout world models and physics engines by treating the learned model itself as an interactive simulator for policy loops.
paper_cards.evidence: Primary evidence comes from the arXiv paper, official RSS project page, public code, and interactive demo; long-horizon runtime claims are source-traced.

claim_checks.claim: The simulator supports stable long-horizon interaction for more than 10 minutes at 15 FPS.
claim_checks.notes: Official project page states the runtime and horizon claim.

claim_checks.claim: The system uses consistency models for both image decoding and latent-space dynamics.
Official code and an interactive demo are public.
claim_checks.notes: Project page links both the GitHub repository and online demo.

paper_cards.limitations: Visual and control quality were judged from the official demo surface and paper rather than independent rollout execution inside this run.
paper_cards.project_relevance: High-value reference for learned world simulators that can sit directly inside embodied training and evaluation loops rather than only generating showcase videos.

paper_cards.title: World Pilot: Steering Vision-Language-Action Models with World-Action Priors
paper_cards.data: LIBERO-Plus and real-robot manipulation evaluations paired with a world-action prior and public Hugging Face model release.
paper_cards.method: injects a World-Action Model into a VLA through latent steering at the perception layer and action steering at the trajectory/action layer.
paper_cards.task: improve manipulation policy quality by giving VLA policies compact anticipatory priors about scene evolution and motion.
paper_cards.novelty: shows a concrete way to route world-model priors into a VLA without forcing slow explicit pixel rollouts at action time.
paper_cards.evidence: Primary evidence comes from the arXiv paper, official project page, GitHub repository, and Hugging Face weights; performance claims are kept source-reported.

claim_checks.claim: World Pilot augments a VLA with world-action priors through latent steering and action steering.
The method reaches source-reported state-of-the-art performance on LIBERO-Plus and real-robot tasks.
claim_checks.notes: Treat exact numbers as source-reported; this run did not reproduce results.

claim_checks.claim: Official code and Hugging Face weights are public.
claim_checks.notes: Project page links both GitHub and Hugging Face.

paper_cards.limitations: Benchmark leadership claims remain source-reported; this run did not rerun LIBERO-Plus or real-robot evaluations.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Excellent fit for the world-action-model branch because it operationalizes how a learned world prior can improve a deployed VLA policy.

paper_cards.title: Being-H0.7: A Latent World-Action Model from Egocentric Videos
paper_cards.data: large-scale egocentric video pretraining paired with robot-control evaluation and public code for a latent world-action model.
paper_cards.method: learns a latent world-action model that carries future-aware interaction structure from egocentric videos into a deployable action prior without explicit pixel rollout at test time.
paper_cards.task: improve robot control by giving policies future-aware latent dynamics and task-progress signals extracted from dense video structure.
paper_cards.novelty: keeps the predictive benefits of world modeling while moving the reasoning substrate from expensive pixel prediction into a compact latent control interface.
paper_cards.evidence: Primary evidence comes from the arXiv paper, official project page, and public GitHub organization; scale and positioning claims are source-traced.

claim_checks.claim: Being-H0.7 is a latent world-action model trained from egocentric videos.
claim_checks.notes: Title and abstract state the latent world-action formulation and egocentric-video data source.

claim_checks.claim: The official project positions the method as preserving world-model predictive value without explicit future-image generation at test time.
claim_checks.notes: Official project text makes this comparison directly.
The Being-H repository is linked from the official project page.

paper_cards.limitations: Exact data scale and downstream robot metrics should be cited from the paper directly; this run did not independently evaluate the released model.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Useful anchor for compact world-action priors that keep embodied reasoning in the control loop without paying full pixel-rollout cost.

paper_cards.title: Cosmos 3: Omnimodal World Models for Physical AI
paper_cards.data: omnimodal physical-AI release surface spanning language, image, video, audio, and action sequences with public model cards and source code.
paper_cards.method: unified mixture-of-transformers world-model family that jointly processes and generates multimodal physical-world sequences, subsuming VLMs, video generators, world simulators, and world-action models.
paper_cards.task: support understanding, generation, simulation, and action inside one omnimodal world-model stack for physical AI use cases.
paper_cards.novelty: collapses several previously separate embodied model classes into one omnimodal world-model family with flexible input-output configurations.
paper_cards.evidence: Primary evidence comes from the arXiv technical report, official NVIDIA Cosmos 3 page, public model-card collection, and official GitHub repository.

claim_checks.claim: Cosmos 3 jointly processes and generates language, image, video, audio, and action sequences in one architecture.
claim_checks.notes: Abstract states the omnimodal scope and unified architecture.

claim_checks.claim: The release surface positions Cosmos 3 as one model family connecting understanding, generation, simulation, and action.
claim_checks.notes: Official NVIDIA page states the shared omnimodal model framing directly.

claim_checks.claim: Official GitHub code and Hugging Face model cards are public.
claim_checks.notes: NVIDIA page links public GitHub code and model-card collection.

paper_cards.limitations: Performance leadership claims remain source-reported and tied to NVIDIA’s evaluation stack; this run did not execute the released models locally.
paper_cards.project_relevance: High-impact anchor for world-model systems that unify perception, simulation, and action rather than treating them as separate modules.
